extracted.title: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?
extracted.venue: arXiv 2611.30483 v1, 23 November 2026, cs.SE; preregistered (OSF); harness, records and scripts on Zenodo, as stated
extracted.inclusion: included (Part A), a judgement for review, recorded for its recoverability outcome only as the brief directs: engine-native undo and vendors' minimum backup setups tested in a laboratory against a fixed library of mistakes
extracted.population: Layer A: 22 scripted mistakes on four relational engines, 792 cells, 874 drill runs; Layer B: agent trials on nine engines with six small open-weight models (not Anthropic's or OpenAI's)
outcome_facts: "Permanent loss of protected rows ranged from 0 of 432 trials on Apache Cassandra, whose default snapshots before TRUNCATE and DROP undid every such loss (measured with a recovery drill added after the first tables and run seconds after the mistake), to 15% on MySQL and SQLite" (abstract)

"The vendors' minimum backup setup (R1) undid every loss of protected rows in the model-free layer on the four relational engines" (abstract); Section 4.3: R1 "removed all permanent canary loss on all four engines"
